figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the Generative Response Model (GRM) framework. (Left) GRM encodes state-action history via a causal transformer and predicts horizon-aggregate response curves (traffic 𝐼𝑡 :𝑇 , cost ̂̄𝐶𝑡 :𝑇 (·), value ̂̄𝑉 𝑡 :𝑇 (·)). Training uses future-sampled supervision, where for each anchor tick 𝑡 we sample future ticks 𝑘 ∼ U{𝑡, . . . ,𝑇 } from offline data and fit curves to realized outcomes. (Right) The min-pacing controller solves two 1D root equations for budget and CPA constraints, then executes 𝛼𝑡 = min{𝛼𝐵, 𝛼𝐶 }.
